F-002.claim: RODAS5P dense output has no tolerance control of the interior (interpolated) error: acceptance is gated only by the endpoint embedded estimate, and no in-tree test measures interpolant accuracy on a stiff problem.
F-002.note: NARROWED by lens a2 and E-03: on the v2 campaign corpus the interpolated-grid error is only 0.70-2.43x (median 1.08) the accepted-step error, so the original impact sentence (dense-arm consumers mainly measure interpolant error) does not hold there. The stiff interior-order numbers quoted by the finder come from a Python replica, not the Rust lane.

F-006.claim: On an accepted output-clipped step the controller returns the requested step unchanged (adaptive.rs:279-282), and because the v2 campaign hard-stops at every point of a uniform 101-point grid, the clipped arm is effectively a fixed-step h = span/100 integrator.
F-006.note: NARROWED by lens a2 and the G1 fix design: the grid-spaced steps follow from the hard-stop policy (output.rs:281-282), not from a wrong controller formula; a growing controller would be clipped identically, rejections still adapt h, and only 26/54 rows are zero-rejection. The clip-neutral behavior is documented as intentional at adaptive.rs:264-267.

F-007.claim: The v2 output-policy admissibility rule (clipped/dense gap <= 0.1 x dense max-grid error) requires about 10% pointwise agreement between the error vectors of two independently stepped trajectories, which correct solvers rarely deliver: it fails in 54/54 committed rows (minimum ratio 0.1245), in 89-94% of same-code-path admissible pairs, and in 88-94% of SciPy Radau pairs.
F-007.note: NARROWED: 'unattainable' was overstated; 2/18 same-path pairs pass.
